patch.value: Context recency is computed from updated_at, so every governance write the project mandates erases the freshness signal it ranks on

computeContextRelevance derives the recency signal by rank-ordering items on updated_at alone (src/sdk/context-relevance.ts:136-153), and recency carries weight 0.35 — tied for the largest single weight in the default vector, behind only claim_focus and ahead of semantic_similarity. updated_at is the timestamp of the last write of any kind, so it cannot distinguish an item that a human or agent actually advanced from an item a sweep touched. Every maintenance operation this project requires — resolution backfill, close-reason backfill, relationship enrichment, release attribution stamping, normalization, duplicate renames — writes updated_at on terminal items and thereby promotes long-finished work to maximal freshness. This is not hypothetical: the release attribution backfill and terminal graph backfill in this same lane rewrote updated_at on 1782 and 1713 items respectively, so the entire terminal corpus now presents as newer than every genuinely active item. The narrow twin of this defect was already fixed once (pm-d9g9 rejected empty appends precisely so they could not fake freshness), which establishes that write-time is not freshness; the general class was never addressed. A maintenance-invariant temporal coordinate now exists in the data: every terminal item carries a stamped release identifier, and the immutable history stream distinguishes substantive operations (create, close, cancel, status transition, claim, comment) from maintenance operations (dependency add, metadata backfill, normalization, redaction, repair).

History operations carry a declared substantive-versus-maintenance classification that is part of the contract surface rather than a heuristic inside the scorer; The recency signal derives from the most recent substantive event for an item, falling back to the stamped release cohort and then to created_at, never to a bare updated_at; A property test proves that applying a pure-maintenance mutation to any item leaves the relevance ordering of the whole workspace unchanged; The classification is exposed so packages and extensions computing their own recency agree with the core definition instead of re-deriving it; Existing recency behaviour is preserved for workspaces with no history, so small and fresh projects degrade to the current ordering exactly; Explain-ranking discloses which event and which class produced the recency component for every scored item
Make temporal relevance a property of what happened to an item, not of when a file holding it was last written
Governance sweeps and relevance ranking stop being mutually exclusive, so the tracker can be maintained without degrading the context it exists to serve
Restores the top-weighted relevance signal across context, next, and search after bulk maintenance, and removes the standing incentive to avoid backfills
Recency derives from classified substantive history events with the release cohort as a stable fallback, and a maintenance sweep provably does not reorder relevance
The mandated terminal-graph and attribution backfills have now touched the whole terminal corpus, so the corruption is live rather than theoretical
